Entry tier accounts

clauses.source: Doc 041 Step 6.1 asks for 'successful unauthorized transactions'. Doc 041 Step 2 names the declined types 'atm_withdrawal_declined'/'pos_declined'. Doc 018 gives status as 'posted' or 'pending'. So successful means the non-declined types, in either status.

clauses.clause: window from the earliest declined attempt to now, plus other recent ones
clauses.source: Doc 041 Step 6.1 refers to 'the suspicious period' without bounds. The declined PIN attempts (Step 2) are what led to the lock. The step bounds the window by them and also asks the customer about other recent transactions, so the gap is covered by a question.

dispute.why: Each argument follows doc 031's field definitions, the category and card_action mappings, doc 032 and the tool description.

clauses.clause: card_present_fraud for an ATM transaction
clauses.source: Doc 031 defines card_present_fraud as 'Physical card used fraudulently ... card was physically present'. Doc 031 lists 'atm_withdrawal' as a transaction made with the card. So an ATM transaction falls under the physical/in-store branch.

clauses.clause: disputed_amount: the absolute recorded amount
clauses.source: Doc 031 defines it as 'The dollar amount being disputed'. Doc 018 records debits as negative. The tool rejects a non-positive value: 'disputed_amount must be a positive number'. So the absolute value is used.

clauses.clause: customer_max_liability_amount: lesser of $50/$500 and the amount, or -1
clauses.source: Doc 031 sets $50, $500 and unlimited tiers by report timing from the statement. The tool says the value is based on 'timing rules and the disputed amount' and 'Use -1 for unlimited'. So the cap is the lesser of the tier figure and the amount.

recommend.why: Doc 041 Step 6.3 lists the three options, recommends closure if fraud is suspected, and the CRITICAL row recommends closure.

clauses.clause: otherwise present the options without recommending one
clauses.source: Doc 041 Step 6.3 recommends closure only 'if fraud suspected', and the threshold table recommends it only for CRITICAL. No passage recommends any option for the other cannot-unlock cases, so holding back a recommendation stays.

pin_lock_close_no_dispute.why: Doc 041 Step 6 files disputes only when unauthorized transactions are found, and doc 025 supplies the reason list and the closing path.

clauses.clause: file no dispute
clauses.source: Doc 041 Step 6.2 files a dispute only 'If unauthorized transactions found'. Step 6.3 (no unauthorized transactions) lists only closure, transfer or PIN reset. So no dispute is filed.

pick_action.why: Doc 031 states the severity order and says to perform the most severe action once per card.

unfiled_dispute_ignored.why: Doc 031 takes the most severe action across disputes after filing them, so an unfiled dispute records no card_action.

clauses.clause: disputes not filed set no card action
clauses.source: Doc 031 says card_action is recorded 'when filing' each dispute, and the actual action is chosen 'after filing all disputes ... across all disputes'. An unfiled dispute has no recorded card_action to count.

alert_card_not_cleared.why: Doc 003 clears a customer-initiated alert only when all transactions are confirmed legitimate, which a filed fraud dispute contradicts, and doc 031 maps fraud disputes to close_and_reissue.

clauses.clause: do not clear the alert
clauses.source: Doc 003: 'If they confirm all transactions are legitimate, clear the alert.' A filed card_present_fraud or card_not_present_fraud dispute means the customer reported a transaction they did not make (doc 031). So the clearing condition is not met.

clauses.clause: close with reason fraud_suspected
clauses.source: Doc 031 maps the fraud categories to 'close_and_reissue', which 'the agent must separately perform'. Doc 025 lists 'Suspected fraud/unauthorized transactions' as reason fraud_suspected.

keep_active.why: Doc 031 maps the keep_active categories to keeping the card active.

found_card_not_closed.why: Doc 026 closes when a card is confirmed lost/stolen or the customer wants to cancel, and lets a card frozen while misplaced be unfrozen.

clauses.clause: do not close a found card for the loss
clauses.source: Doc 026: 'CLOSE ... Use when card is confirmed lost/stolen or customer wants to cancel.' A found card is no longer confirmed lost, and the customer has not asked to cancel. So neither closing condition holds.

clauses.clause: unfreeze it if they want
clauses.source: Doc 026 freezes when the 'Customer misplaced the card and is looking for it', and says the card 'can be unfrozen later' under the unfreezing requirements. The unfreeze tool acts only on FROZEN cards, so an already CLOSED card is not reactivated (doc 025 'Closed cards cannot be reopened').

ask_reason.why: Doc 025 closing step 2 and its reason list state this.

per_card_independent.why: Doc 025 requirements are stated for each card, and doc 029 sets tier rules per checking account.

clauses.clause: a card failing a check does not stop the others
clauses.source: Doc 025 requirements 2-6 each test 'the debit card' (its owner, status, transactions, date_issued). Doc 029 tiers belong to each card's checking account. So each card's result is decided separately.

pending_refund_ack.why: Doc 025 requirement 5 states the wait-or-acknowledge choice.

clauses.clause: a pending refund is a pending credit
clauses.source: Doc 018: positive amounts are credits, and status may be 'pending'. A refund returns money in. So a pending refund is a pending positive transaction.

clauses.clause: if they choose to wait, do not close
clauses.source: Doc 025 req 5: the card 'must not have any pending refunds' unless the customer acknowledges in writing. Waiting leaves the refund pending, so the requirement is unmet, and step 3 says 'do not proceed with closure'.

check_elig.why: Each check is a doc 025 requirement, and the FROZEN handling follows from requirement 3 and doc 026's unfreeze.

clauses.clause: a FROZEN card is unfrozen first
clauses.source: Doc 025 req 3 needs ACTIVE or PENDING, and the close tool rejects other statuses. Doc 026 lets a FROZEN card be unfrozen for a verified owner with an OPEN account, and says it is then 'active'. Doc 026 also says CLOSE is used 'when ... customer wants to cancel'. So unfreezing resolves requirement 3.

clauses.clause: no pending transactions other than refunds
clauses.source: Doc 025 req 4 bars pending transactions. Req 5 gives pending refunds their own rule, with an acknowledgment path. So check 3 excludes refunds.

clauses.clause: checks 1 to 4 still apply to lost, stolen and fraud_suspected
clauses.source: Doc 025 step 4: 'These reasons bypass the minimum card age requirement (requirement 6)'. It names only requirement 6, and step 3 says 'If any requirement is not met ... do not proceed with closure'.

clauses.clause: a CLOSED card cannot be closed again; tell the customer
clauses.source: Doc 025 req 3 allows only ACTIVE or PENDING. The close tool returns 'Only ACTIVE or PENDING cards can be closed'. So the agent explains that the card is already closed.

blocked_pending_tx.why: Doc 025 requirement 4 blocks closure until transactions settle, and only requirement 6 is waived for security reasons.

clauses.clause: do not close, whatever the reason
clauses.source: Doc 025 waives only 'requirement 6' for lost/stolen/fraud_suspected. Against that, step 4 'Inform customer that any pending transactions will still be processed' and 'closed immediately with no cooling-off period' could be read as allowing closure. No passage names pending transactions as waived, so the prohibition stays.

clauses.clause: FROZEN card stays frozen
clauses.source: No passage says to unfreeze a card that cannot yet be closed. Doc 026 unfreezing is for a customer who wants it unfrozen, so the hold on unfreezing stays.

clauses.clause: ask whether to freeze an ACTIVE card meanwhile
clauses.source: Doc 026: FREEZE is for when the customer 'wants temporary security', and its reasons include 'Suspicious activity noticed, wants to investigate before closing'. The card cannot be closed yet (doc 025 req 4). The step only asks the customer.

clauses.clause: no settlement time promised
clauses.source: No document gives a settlement time for pending transactions, so none is promised.

blocked_offer_freeze.why: Doc 026 freezing steps 3-4 and requirements (owner, ACTIVE) state this, gated on the customer's agreement.

inform_pending.why: Doc 025 closing step 4 states all three notices for lost, stolen and fraud_suspected.

pin_lock_close_once.why: Doc 041 Step 6.2 closes the card after disputes, doc 025 gives the reason, and closing once follows from the closure being permanent.

clauses.clause: close only once
clauses.source: Doc 025: a closed card is 'permanently deactivated', and the close tool rejects non-ACTIVE/PENDING cards. So a card already closed by the dispute job goes straight to confirmation.

unfreeze_before_close.why: Doc 025 requirement 3 and doc 026's unfreezing requirements and tool support reactivating a FROZEN card so it can be closed.

clauses.clause: unfreeze to close
clauses.source: Doc 025 req 3: closure needs ACTIVE or PENDING. Doc 026 unfreezing requires owner, FROZEN status and an OPEN linked account, and the card is then active. Doc 026 says CLOSE is used when the customer wants to cancel.

clauses.clause: if the unfreeze fails, do not close
clauses.source: No passage decides closing after a failed unfreeze, and the close tool rejects FROZEN cards, so the prohibition stays.

close_card.why: Doc 025 names the tool and reason values, doc 041 Step 6 ties closure to unauthorized transactions or the customer's choice, and the reason follows doc 025's list.

close.why: Doc 025 step 5 names the tool, and doc 031 requires performing close_and_reissue.

clauses.clause: close when pick_action gave close_and_reissue
clauses.source: Doc 031: 'the agent must separately perform the indicated card action after filing the dispute'. Its mapping gives close_and_reissue, which means 'Close card and issue replacement'.

close_frozen_stolen.why: Doc 025 closes lost or stolen cards immediately with those reasons, after the card has been returned to ACTIVE.

confirm_close.why: Doc 025 closing step 6 lists the three confirmations, and Important Notes adds the password recommendation for fraud_suspected.

note_closure_time.why: Doc 029 counts the Entry 48-hour wait from card closure, and the policy requires get_current_time for the current time.

clauses.clause: record the closure time
clauses.source: Doc 029: '48-hour waiting period after card closure'. Policy: 'always use the get_current_time() tool'. So the time read right after closing starts the wait.

freeze_check.why: Doc 026 freezing requirements and its lost/stolen note state this.

freeze_card.why: Doc 026 freezing steps 3-5 state this, and doc 031 maps the action to freeze_debit_card_3892.

offer_replacement.why: Doc 025 step 4 asks about a replacement for lost/stolen/fraud_suspected, the damaged reason implies the customer wants one, and step 6 covers other reasons.

clauses.clause: damaged: confirm the replacement
clauses.source: Doc 025 lists the reason as 'Damaged card (customer wants replacement)'. So a replacement is confirmed with the customer rather than offered.

no_replacement_while_blocked.why: Ordering while the old card stays active is barred by doc 023 requirement 5 and the order tool, and no passage permits it for an unclosed frozen card.

clauses.clause: do not order while the old card is not closed
clauses.source: Doc 023 req 5 ('cannot have more than 1 active debit cards') and the tool error 'already has an active debit card' bar an ACTIVE old card. Doc 029 frames replacement as following 'card closure'. Against that, doc 023's note that the existing card 'will remain active until the new card is activated' could be read as allowing an order. No passage names a blocked or frozen card, so the hold stays.

replacement_check.why: Doc 023 eligibility and doc 029 replacement counting and tier limits state each check.

clauses.clause: limit reached counts as at the limit
clauses.source: Doc 029 allows a 'Maximum 2/3/5 replacement cards per rolling 12-month period'. With that many already counted, a new one would exceed the maximum, so the fee-or-wait rule applies.

entry_wait.why: Doc 029 sets the Entry 48-hour wait counted from card closure.

clauses.clause: earliest order time = closure time + 48 hours
clauses.source: Doc 029: '48-hour waiting period after card closure'. Adding 48 hours to the closure time recorded in note_closure_time gives the earliest time.

entry_fee_then_wait.why: Doc 029 gives Entry the wait-or-$25 choice, charges fees when the card is ordered, and keeps the 48-hour wait as a separate Entry rule.

clauses.clause: 48-hour wait still applies after accepting the fee
clauses.source: Doc 029's Entry list gives the 48-hour wait and the excess-fee option as separate rules. The fee option answers only the limit. So the wait remains.

over_limit_customer_waits.why: The age-out date and the Entry combination follow from doc 029's rolling window, date_issued counting and 48-hour wait.

clauses.clause: ages out 12 months after date_issued
clauses.source: Doc 029 counts cards by date_issued 'within the last 12 months' over a 'rolling 12-month period'. So the oldest counted card leaves the window 12 months after its date_issued.

clauses.clause: Entry earliest date is the later of the two
clauses.source: Doc 029 requires both the Entry 48-hour wait and staying within the limit. The order is possible only when both are met, which is the later date.

clauses.clause: order nothing and charge no fee now
clauses.source: Doc 029 charges fees 'when the card is ordered'. Choosing to wait means no order now, so no fee is charged.

tier.why: Doc 005 maps account names to tiers, and doc 029 sets fees by those tiers.

clauses.clause: account name to tier mapping
clauses.source: Doc 005 lists ENTRY (Light Blue, Light Green, Green Fee-Free), MID (Blue, Green), PREMIUM (Evergreen) and ELITE (Bluest). Doc 029 uses the same tier names for replacement fees.

ask_prefs.why: Doc 023 steps 4-6 and doc 029's fee notice state this.

ask_options.why: Every fee figure is stated in doc 029, and the address and fee notices in docs 023 and 029.

clauses.clause: no RUSH option listed for Mid
clauses.source: Doc 029 lists only 'Standard ... or expedited shipping' for Mid. Doc 023 lists RUSH generally with 'fees may vary based on account tier' but does not name Mid. So holding back a Mid RUSH offer stays.

mid_expedited_with_fee.why: Doc 029 states the Mid $15 expedited fee and doc 023 the 3-5 day timeframe.

entry_expedited_request.why: Doc 029 limits Entry to standard shipping with a 48-hour wait, and doc 023 gives the 7-10 day timeframe.

best_free_options.why: The choices are the fastest $0 delivery and the upgraded $0 design for each tier in doc 029.

clauses.clause: best free = fastest $0 delivery and upgraded $0 design
clauses.source: Doc 023 gives timeframes RUSH 1-2 < EXPEDITED 3-5 < STANDARD 7-10. Doc 029 gives $0 delivery: Premium STANDARD/EXPEDITED, Elite all, Mid/Entry STANDARD. Doc 029 gives $0 design: Premium CLASSIC/PREMIUM, Elite all, Mid/Entry CLASSIC.

fastest_free_option.why: Doc 029 gives the $0 delivery options per tier, doc 023 the timeframes, and CLASSIC is the default.

clauses.clause: fastest $0 delivery per tier
clauses.source: Doc 023 timeframes, combined with doc 029's $0 delivery per tier, give Elite RUSH, Premium EXPEDITED, and Mid/Entry STANDARD.

fastest_paid_option.why: Doc 029 states the tier fees, and paid options wait for the customer's acceptance of the fee.

clauses.clause: Mid fastest is EXPEDITED
clauses.source: Doc 029 lists only standard and expedited for Mid, while doc 023 lists RUSH generally without naming Mid. So the hold on offering Mid RUSH stays.

design_if_free.why: The rule follows from doc 029's tier design fees and doc 023's CLASSIC default.

clauses.clause: fall back to CLASSIC
clauses.source: Doc 023: 'CLASSIC ... (default, no fee)'. Doc 029: CLASSIC is $0 in every tier.

alternate_mailing_address.why: Doc 023 step 6 confirms the mailing address, and requirement 9 says international shipping is not available.

clauses.clause: check the address is in the US
clauses.source: Doc 023 req 9: 'international shipping is not available'. So an alternate address must also be domestic.

order.why: Doc 023 step 7 and doc 029's exact-fee, excess-fee and wait rules state each argument and condition.

confirm_order.why: Doc 023 step 8 and its delivery timeframes state this.

cross_product_handoff.why: Doc 030 applies to a reported lost or stolen card after the freeze or close procedure.

action_error.why: Doc 042 gives technical_system_error, doc 003 escalates persistent errors, and the policy requires the customer's consent before a transfer.

R4.why: Doc 025 requirement 5 states the wait-or-acknowledge choice.

R12.why: Doc 029 Premium design fees state this.

R14.why: Doc 029 gives the Entry fee-or-wait choice and the separate 48-hour wait.

R27.why: Doc 029 gives no waiting period for Mid, Premium and Elite.

R31.why: Doc 023 gives RUSH at $35 and 1-2 days with tier-varying fees, and doc 029 sets Elite RUSH to $0.

R32.why: Doc 041 Step 6.3 offers closure as one option among several when no unauthorized transactions are found.

verdicts.unsupported: Unlock; status, issue_reason and date_issued
verdicts.why: The quote supports calling the tool for the checking account, but the visible field list stops after card_id and account_id and nothing quoted mentions unlocking the tool.

verdicts.clause: all
verdicts.why: The ENTRY TIER passage sets a 48-hour wait after card closure before a replacement can be ordered and says standard shipping only, so giving the earliest time and not ordering now follow.

verdicts.clause: only STANDARD delivery is available ($0, 7-10 business days)
verdicts.unsupported: 7-10 business days
verdicts.why: The ENTRY quote gives standard shipping only at delivery_fee $0, but no quote for this step states the 7-10 business day transit time.

verdicts.clause: $15 from checking, 3-5 business days
verdicts.unsupported: from checking, 3-5 business days
verdicts.why: The MID quote gives expedited at delivery_fee $15, but it says nothing about charging checking or a 3-5 business day transit time.

verdicts.why: derived: the MID quote offers Standard at $0 or expedited at $15, so making the choice depend on the customer accepting the fee is a question for the customer.

verdicts.clause: Premium RUSH $35; Elite RUSH $0; Mid EXPEDITED $15; Entry STANDARD only
verdicts.unsupported: Elite RUSH $0; Mid EXPEDITED $15; Entry STANDARD only; that RUSH is the quickest
verdicts.why: The quote supports only Premium rush at $35; the visible Elite text is cut off before its fees, and no quote for this step gives the Mid or Entry options or ranks speeds.

verdicts.clause: Use a paid option only after the customer accepts the fee
verdicts.why: Fee acceptance is a question put to the customer, not a document rule.

verdicts.clause: Elite RUSH, Premium EXPEDITED, Mid ... STANDARD
verdicts.why: derived: the tier quotes say Elite pays $0 for RUSH, Premium $0 for EXPEDITED and Mid $0 only for Standard, and doc 023 ranks RUSH (1-2 days) above EXPEDITED (3-5) above STANDARD (7-10).

verdicts.clause: Entry STANDARD
verdicts.unsupported: Entry
verdicts.why: No quote for this step gives Entry tier shipping; only doc 023's general 'STANDARD: Free shipping' supports a $0 standard option, with no Entry-specific rule.

verdicts.clause: Mid and Entry have only CLASSIC at $0
verdicts.why: derived: the CLASSIC quote and its surrounding ENTRY and MID design lists put CLASSIC at $0, PREMIUM at $10 and CUSTOM at $25.

verdicts.clause: For Premium, CLASSIC and PREMIUM are both $0; for Elite, CLASSIC, PREMIUM and CUSTOM are all $0
verdicts.why: derived: the PREMIUM and CUSTOM complimentary quotes and their surrounding text give these fees, with Premium CUSTOM at $15.

verdicts.clause: ask the customer which free design they want. Both fees are 0
verdicts.why: derived: asking which design is a question for the customer, and choosing a $0 delivery with a $0 design makes both fees 0.

ensure_verified.why: Doc 023 requirement 1 and the policy's verification and no-reverification rules state both branches.

per_account.why: Each order is tied to one specified checking account, and the replacement rules depend on that account's tier, so the steps run once per account.

clauses.clause: run the steps below once per account, each with its own tier, and ask delivery and design separately for each
clauses.source: 1) Doc 023 step 2: confirm which checking account the card should be linked to. 2) Doc 023 steps 3-5: eligibility, delivery and design are handled for 'the specified account'. 3) Doc 029: replacement policies 'vary based on the customer's checking account tier'. 4) So each account gets its own checks, tier, delivery and design.

get_accounts.why: Doc 009 names the tool and the fields it returns.

get_cards.why: Doc 028 names the tool and the status, issue_reason and date_issued fields.

get_user.why: The tool description returns DOB and address, which doc 023 requirements 7 and 9 need.

get_time.why: The policy requires get_current_time whenever the current time is needed, and the 3-business-day, 12-month and 48-hour checks need it.

clauses.clause: current time for the business-day, 12-month and 48-hour checks
clauses.source: 1) Doc 023 requirement 4: open at least 3 business days. 2) Doc 029: rolling 12-month count and Entry 48-hour wait. 3) Policy guideline 4: always use get_current_time() for the current time.

check_order.why: Each check is a doc 023 eligibility requirement, and the active/pending check follows from requirements 5 and 8, doc 028 and the order tool's error.

clauses.clause: there is no other ACTIVE or PENDING card
clauses.source: 1) Doc 023 requirement 5: no more than 1 active card per checking account. 2) Doc 023 requirement 8: no PENDING card for the account. 3) Doc 028 use case 1: before ordering, check for an active or pending card. 4) The order_debit_card_5739 description: 'already has an active debit card. Maximum 1 active card per checking account.'

clauses.clause: If a check fails, explain what blocks the order and stop
clauses.source: 1) Doc 023 lists these as eligibility requirements and step 3 checks them before ordering. 2) Failing a requirement means the account is not eligible, so no order is placed. 3) Withholding the write is also kept.

old_card_not_closed.why: No passage permits ordering while the old card's closure is blocked; the prohibition is kept, and the message follows from docs 025 and 029.

clauses.clause: do not order
clauses.source: Doc 023's note that 'the customer's existing debit card (if any) will remain active until the new card is activated' could be read to allow ordering. The order tool's 'Maximum 1 active card' error and doc 028 use case 1 point the other way. No passage names a blocked closure, so the prohibition stays.

clauses.clause: a new card can be ordered once the old card is closed
clauses.source: 1) Doc 025 step 6: after closure, 'If they need a new card, they can order one through the standard ordering process'. 2) Doc 029: Mid, Premium and Elite 'can order immediately after closure'; Entry after 48 hours.

tier.why: Doc 029 uses checking account tiers it does not define, and doc 005 is the passage that maps the named checking accounts to those tiers.

clauses.clause: Light Blue, Light Green, Green Fee-Free ENTRY; Blue, Green MID; Evergreen PREMIUM; Bluest ELITE
clauses.source: 1) Doc 029 applies ENTRY/MID/PREMIUM/ELITE rules by 'the customer's checking account tier'. 2) Doc 005 assigns the checking accounts to these tier names: ENTRY (Light Blue, Light Green, Green Fee-Free), MID (Blue, Green (checking)), PREMIUM (Evergreen), ELITE (Bluest).

history.why: Doc 029 states the counted reasons, the 12-month window and each tier's limit and remedy.

clauses.clause: At the limit
clauses.source: 1) Doc 029: 'Maximum N replacement cards per rolling 12-month period'. 2) With N counted replacements, the requested card would be N+1, which exceeds the maximum. 3) So the 'exceeded the N-card limit' remedy applies when the count reaches N.

excess_fee_choice_step.why: Doc 029 states the wait-or-pay choice and fees for Entry and Mid, and the fee-deduction notice before ordering.

clauses.clause: give the date the oldest counted card ages out
clauses.source: 1) Doc 029: they must 'wait until oldest replacement ages out of the 12-month window'. 2) Doc 029 history step 3: count by date_issued within the last 12 months. 3) So the date is the oldest counted date_issued plus 12 months.

wait_date.why: The age-out date follows from the 12-month window, and the Entry date also has to meet the separate 48-hour rule.

clauses.clause: age-out date is the oldest counted card's date_issued plus 12 months
clauses.source: 1) Doc 029: wait until oldest replacement ages out of the 12-month window. 2) Doc 029: count by date_issued within the last 12 months. 3) The oldest card leaves the window 12 months after its date_issued.

clauses.clause: For Entry, use the later of that date and the closure time plus 48 hours
clauses.source: 1) Doc 029 Entry: '48-hour waiting period after card closure before a replacement can be ordered'. 2) Doc 029 Entry: over the limit, wait for age-out. 3) Both must hold, so the earliest order is the later of the two.

entry_wait.why: Doc 029 states the Entry 48-hour wait after closure and the standard-only shipping.

clauses.clause: Give the earliest time
clauses.source: Doc 029 Entry: 48-hour waiting period after card closure, so the earliest time is the closure time plus 48 hours.

entry_expedited_request.why: Doc 029 Entry states 'Standard shipping only (no expedited option available) - delivery_fee: $0', and doc 023 gives STANDARD as 7-10 business days.

excess_fee_then_wait.why: The fee only replaces the age-out wait, the 48-hour wait is a separate Entry rule, and fees are charged when the card is ordered.

clauses.clause: the 48-hour wait still blocks the order after the fee is accepted
clauses.source: 1) Doc 029 Entry lists the 48-hour wait after closure as its own rule. 2) Doc 029: the $25 fee is the alternative only to waiting for the oldest replacement to age out. 3) So the 48-hour wait still applies.

clauses.clause: the fee will be charged when they order then
clauses.source: Doc 029: all fees, including the excess replacement fee, are 'AUTOMATICALLY CHARGED to the linked checking account when the card is ordered'.

ask_delivery.why: Fees and times are stated in docs 029 and 023; leaving RUSH out for Mid holds back an offer no passage decides.

clauses.clause: Mid: STANDARD $0, EXPEDITED $15 (no RUSH offered)
clauses.source: Doc 029 Mid lists only 'Standard ... or expedited shipping available', while doc 023 lists RUSH $35 generally with 'fees may vary based on account tier'. No passage names RUSH for Mid, so the held-back offer stays.

mid_expedited_with_fee.why: Doc 029 states the Mid $15 expedited fee and doc 023 the 3-5 day time; paying only on acceptance follows the inform-before-ordering rule.

clauses.clause: Use EXPEDITED only if the customer accepts; otherwise STANDARD
